v.why: Adding the input-to-output residual where none existed gives a larger gain than swapping out an existing conv or pool on that edge.
Removing the residual skip on edge 0->3 hurts optimization much more than removing a conv or avg-pool there.
Filling an empty 0->3 edge with a conv adds capacity, while replacing an existing skip with a conv destroys the beneficial residual path.
With edge 0->2 already absent, cutting 0->1 disconnects nodes 1 and 2 from the input and collapses most of the cell.
When edge 0 is none, node 1 is dead, so adding a conv revives edges 2 and 4 as well and yields a larger gain than upgrading a skip or pool.
If edge 0->1 is none, node 1 carries only zeros, so a conv on 1->2 adds nothing.
With edge 2->3 removed, node 2 never reaches the output, so improving its input edge has no effect.
Deleting a useful 3x3 conv costs more accuracy than deleting a weak avg-pool or a redundant skip.
Avg-pool edges are typically harmful in NAS-Bench-201, so removing one helps or barely hurts, while removing a conv or skip hurts.
Putting avg-pool on an empty edge is near-neutral, but swapping it in for a strong 3x3 conv on 2->3 clearly reduces accuracy.
